secondary.name: decima
secondary.model_identifier_choices_note: Decima accepts 'ensemble' (the published 4-replicate list rep0..rep3), any single replicate name ('rep0'..'rep3'), or an explicit list of replicate names for a custom-size ensemble. A single replicate (rep0) is used here so a full main.py run completes within a 3-day CPU budget on this Mac. The published ensemble averages 4 replicates to reduce per-variant prediction variance; using 1 replicate increases that variance but does not change the sign of effect predictions. The degu_style_ensemble_disagreement selector in evaluation.selectors becomes vacuous and is reported as such in evaluation.json. Audit this deviation from the published ensemble when reporting results.
secondary.device_note: CPU is used instead of MPS because the 4-replicate ensemble exceeds the 12 GB MPS unified-memory ceiling on the development Mac, and the 2-replicate ensemble still exceeds a safe MPS budget once activations are added. CPU inference is slower per variant but has no hard accelerator-memory cap.
secondary.num_workers_note: CPU inference with the 4-replicate ensemble is memory-bound, not CPU-bound. One DataLoader worker avoids forking the ~8 GB of resident ensemble weights and the hg38 FASTA across multiple spawn processes.
secondary.batch_size_note: Decima inputs are 524,288-bp one-hot sequences; CPU activation peaks at batch_size>1 push a 4-replicate ensemble past Apple-silicon RAM. Keep batch_size=1 until the ensemble is reduced.
secondary.weights_source: Zenodo 15092691 (fetched automatically by decima.hub.load_decima_model via HuggingFace)
secondary.status: Decima (Genentech 2026); frozen inference-only, published 4-replicate ensemble on CPU. Replicate weights are downloaded on first use and cached by Decima/HF. Reference FASTA is read from the project directory decima_cache_dir.

primary_T.note: 242 of 8856 Decima tasks match. Matches the Ho target context and both Bourges contexts.

jurkat.query: cell_type in ['CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell', 'mature NK T cell', 'gd T cell', 'mucosal invariant T cell']
jurkat.note: Decima has no Jurkat or cell-line task (0 of 8856 match jurkat/leukaemia/lymphoma/T-ALL), so the previous stanza set this column to a structural zero for every variant via proxy_zero, carrying no information. Jurkat is an immortalised T-lymphoblast line, so this state now queries real non-CD4 T-lymphocyte tasks (CD8 259, mature NK T 173, gd T 12, MAIT 87 = 531 tasks) as its nearest biological analogue. These are deliberately DISJOINT from the primary_T query (CD4-positive), so the two Ho contexts remain distinguishable rather than duplicating one column. on_missing is fail, so a silent zero-fill can no longer occur. This is a declared proxy: Jurkat is a transformed line and these are primary T subsets, so the state is a lineage approximation, not a cell-line match.

b_cell.query: cell_type in ['B cell', 'naive B cell', 'memory B cell']
b_cell.note: 474 of 8856 Decima tasks match. GM12878 is an EBV-transformed lymphoblastoid B-cell line.

secondary.task_queries_note: Each cell state in framework.cell_states must have a stanza here with: query (pandas .query() expression against decima.hub.load_decima_metadata().obs), on_missing ('fail' | 'proxy_zero'), proxy (short tag that reaches audit.json when a proxy is substituted). Resolved task counts are written to audit.json -> decima.per_state[state].task_count.

jurkat.label: Jurkat T lymphoblast cell line
jurkat.note: Kept as a distinct state so the Ho source context (Jurkat) and target context (primary T) never collapse onto one cell state. K562 is aliased here as the haematopoietic source of the development pair. Decima has no Jurkat task, so this state uses a T-lymphoblast proxy query (see task_queries).

fusion.tracks_coverage_policy_note: disable_if_incomplete keeps every variant and drops the tracks block for any dataset without full NPZ coverage. Chosen because the Siraj track download is truncated, not random: chromosomes 11-19 have 100% coverage, chr10 94%, chr1 32%, and chr2-9, 20, 21, 22 and X have 0%. restrict_to_covered would have cut the development cohort from 197,573 to 88,383 rows and, critically, from 1,564 to 549 independent loci across only 11 of 23 chromosomes, which is the unit of the locus-grouped CV and bootstrap. The covered and uncovered pools are statistically indistinguishable (target variance 0.234 vs 0.251, |z|>3 sign agreement 0.996 vs 0.994, identical median SE), so the restriction carried no scientific benefit; the tracks block itself was worth only 0.007 precision-weighted R2. Ho retains tracks regardless (18,133 NPZs for 18,134 variants), so the held-out evaluation is unaffected.
fusion.track_cell_states_note: The AlphaGenome track block covers ONLY these cell states, which is deliberately a subset of cell_states. All 173,589 cached NPZs were downloaded against the earlier two-state configuration and contain exactly the keys 'primary_T:<modality>' and 'jurkat:<modality>'. The config now also declares b_cell for Decima, but no cached NPZ holds 'b_cell:*', and the loader raises KeyError on a missing key rather than fabricating a zero. Restricting the track block to the two states that have real measured data keeps the block live without inventing values. Decima still scores all three states. To extend tracks to b_cell, rerun scripts/download_alphagenome_tracks.py with the current cell_states and add b_cell to this list.

head.precision_weight_note: Target head is fitted with weights 1/target_se^2 (mean-normalised). Half the Ho rows hold only 5.5% of target variance; weighting raises precision-weighted R2 from 0.0146 to 0.0267 [0.0210, 0.0342]. Uses the reported measurement error only, never the effect size.

rough_soft_ai_rejected_variant_value.note: Rough-soft AI must output a number for every held-out variant. For variants where the VPRS lower approximation is empty (model declines), we define the Rough-soft AI prediction to equal the source-context effect (Jurkat), i.e. 'no evidence of a cell-type change'. This is a definition of the Rough-soft AI method, not an error fallback.

evaluation.development_context_pair_note: K562 (erythroleukaemia) -> GM12878 (lymphoblastoid B cell). Both are haematopoietic, so the development cohort shares lineage with the held-out Ho (Jurkat -> primary CD4+ T) and Bourges (resting -> stimulated primary T) cohorts, and the AlphaGenome track ontologies and Decima cell states requested by this config (CD4+ T cell, Jurkat) are biologically appropriate for it. Selected over the higher-correlation HepG2 -> HCT116 pair (r=0.539, R2prec=0.503) because that pair is endoderm epithelium and would make every foundation-model block a cross-lineage mismatch. Measured for K562 -> GM12878: n=157,084 across 1,894 independent loci and 22 chromosomes (MORE loci than HepG2 -> HCT116, which has 1,538), r=0.202, precision-weighted CV R2=0.085, sign agreement 0.927 among variants with |z|>3 in both contexts, OLS slope 0.319 confirming context-specific magnitude. CAVEAT: all Siraj contexts share one plasmid pool, so source and target errors are correlated (log plasmid depth r=1.000, Skew_SE r=0.880); Siraj cross-context R2 is therefore partly technical and must not be reported as a biological generalisation result. Ho and Bourges provide the independent-error estimate.
evaluation.expert_alone_selection_note: Expert-alone selects its own B variants to review using a non-VPRS rule, so that the Expert-alone vs Neurojico comparison tests whether VPRS boundary selection beats a reasonable uncertainty-blind selection rule under the same reviewed-variant budget.
evaluation.feature_ablations_note: Each entry re-fits the Ridge head and VPRS on the listed feature blocks and reports the four-method RMSE on the same held-out folds, so the contribution of each block (and of per-cell-state tracks once available) is measured directly.
